shell.robotAlt: AI Explorer robot showing Token connections

labels.updatedIncludesContext: now includes information from the surrounding context
labels.simplifiedNotNumbers: The colours only help us picture the idea. A real model updates many numerical values.

page2.idea1: Focus on one target Token, such as “dog”.
page2.idea4: The diagram is a teaching picture.

page1.title: Meet the Transformer
page1.subtitle: Watch other visible Tokens add information to one Token.
page1.question: What happens to the visible Tokens?
page1.intro: Lesson 2 showed which Tokens the model can currently use. A Transformer can now combine information between those Token positions.
page1.tokenLabel: The tired dog slept beside the warm fire.
page1.before: The Token “dog” starts with its own information
page1.step1: The Token “tired” sends descriptive information towards “dog”.
page1.step2: The Token “slept” adds information about what happened.
page1.step3: The Token “beside” is shown as a lighter contribution in this classroom example.
page1.changedExplanation: The Token “dog” now carries information from other Tokens in the Context Window.
page1.literalNote: The words are not literally glued together. The model updates numerical Token representations.
page1.technical: A Transformer is the main processing system inside many modern language models. It lets Token positions use information from other visible Token positions.
page1.takeaway: The Token “dog” started with its own representation. The Transformer used visible context to update it.
page1.bridge: The Transformer can connect Tokens. But do all connections contribute equally?

page2.title: Some connections contribute more
page2.subtitle: Compare how visible Tokens contribute to the current Token.
page2.question: Do all Token connections contribute equally?
page2.intro: Keep the same sentence and focus on the Token “dog”. Reveal a simplified picture of how nearby Tokens can contribute different amounts of information.
page2.lastPage: Last page: Tokens can share information.
page2.now: Now: some connections contribute more than others.
page2.diagramQuestion: Do all visible Tokens contribute equally to the Token “dog”?
page2.connectionLabel: The target Token “dog” is in the centre, with stronger links from “tired” and “slept” and a lighter link from “beside”
page2.whyExplanation: For this example, the Tokens “slept” and “tired” tell us more about “dog” than “beside” does.
page2.takeaway: Useful connections depend on the Tokens and the current processing step.
page2.technical: Attention is one mechanism inside a Transformer that helps combine information from different Token positions. Different connections can contribute different amounts. This classroom diagram shows the idea, not real model values.
page2.accuracy: Teaching picture — not real Qwen attention weights. A real Transformer calculates these relationships numerically.
page2.bridge: Next, use those connections to update one Token representation.

page3.title: Build a context-aware Token
page3.subtitle: Add context information to a simplified Token representation.
page3.question: What changes when Tokens connect?
page3.intro: Lesson 1 showed that Tokens are turned into numerical representations. Now the Transformer updates those representations using context.
page3.controlsLabel: Add context contributions to the Token “dog”
page3.complete: The representation of the Token “dog” now carries information from this context.
page3.technical: A contextual representation is the updated numerical representation of a Token after information from the current context has been combined.
page3.takeaway: After contextual processing, a Token representation carries information from the current context.
page3.bridge: The Token positions also help determine which relationships are being built.

page4.title: Position changes relationships
page4.subtitle: The same Tokens in a new order can build a different relationship.
page4.question: Why does Token order matter?
page4.intro: Switch between two sentences. The Token set is nearly the same, but the positions change who performs the action.
page4.resultA: At position 2, the Token “dog” connects through “chased” to “cat”.
page4.resultB: At position 2, the Token “cat” connects through “chased” to “dog”.
page4.technical: Position information helps the model distinguish where each Token appears in the sequence.
page4.takeaway: The same Tokens in a different order can build different relationships.
page4.bridge: Now watch connections, contribution and updates work together in one process.

page5.title: Several Tokens can update one Token together
page5.subtitle: Watch information from different positions flow into the same Token representation.
page5.question: How can several Tokens update one representation?
page5.intro: Use the reviewed sentence “The robot picked up the red key.” Choose a target and run the four-stage teaching demonstration.
page5.progressLabel: Four stages of the simplified context process
page5.step1: Tokens are available inside the Context Window
page5.step4: The target gets an updated representation
page5.waiting: Ready to combine information for this target.
page5.ready: The target representation now carries information from several Token positions.
page5.technical: Context, connections, contribution strengths and updated representations work as one process before prediction.
page5.accuracy: Simplified teaching visual — real model dimensions do not have simple labels like these, and these are not Qwen hidden states.
page5.takeaway: Several visible Tokens can contribute to one updated Token representation.
page5.bridge: The processed context is now ready to enter the prediction step.

page6.title: What happens before prediction?
page6.subtitle: Connect the four stages that prepare context for Lesson 4.
page6.question: What is ready before the model predicts?
page6.intro: Follow the route from available Tokens to the gate that opens next-token prediction.
page6.predictionNote: Processed context is ready to score possible next Tokens.
page6.point1: Tokens inside the Context Window can contribute information.
page6.point2: A Transformer combines information between Token positions.
page6.point4: Contextual processing prepares the model for next-token prediction.
page6.next: Lesson 4 opens the gate and compares possible next Tokens.
